full_judgment:
5. The prosecution examined ten P.Ws. all of whom were cross-examined by the defence. After close of the prosecution witnesses, the accused on dock were examined under Section 304 of the Code of Criminal Procedure to which they repeated their innocence. The defence did not adduce any evidence. 

 7. The learned Trial Court thereafter in consideration of the evidence on record as well as facts and circumstances of the case found the accused-appellants guilty for the offence charged and convicted them there-under and sentenced to suffer imprisonment for the period as well as ordered to pay a tine with a default clause as mentioned above. The learned Trial Court, however, found the rest six accused not guilty for the offence charged and as such acquitted them therefrom. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied thereby the accused as appellants have come up with the present appeal which is opposed by the respondent-State through the learned Assistant Attorney General Mr. Md. Rabiul Karim. 

 8. Mr. Fazlul Huq Khan Farid, the learned Advocate for the appellants, took us through the F.I.R., charge-sheet, depositions of the prosecution witnesses, impugned judgment and other material papers/documents as available in paper book and submits that this is a case of no evidence. He further submits that the prosecution embellished its case stage by stage and as such the evidence of P.Ws. cannot be relied upon. He finally submits that the unnatural death of the deceased has not been proved inasmuch as non-examination of the doctor who allegedly performed the postmortem examination has made the prosecution case unworthy to believe. He lastly submits that the prosecution even failed to bring the postmortem examination report to show the injuries sustained by the deceased at the hands of the accused-appellants as alleged in compliance with the provisions of Section 509A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and as such he contends that the unnatural death of the deceased having not been proved, the impugned judgment and order of conviction is liable to be set aside. 

 14. P.W. 10 happens to be the investigating officer of this case said about his investigation. He proved the sketch-map with separate index of the place of occurrences and admitted in cross that he did not seize any alamat of this case. This P.W. then said in cross-examination that none of the private P.Ws. said about seeing the occurrence personally by them nor they (witnesses) ever gave any vivid description about the individual act so done by the accused persons. This is all about the evidence on record. 

 15. It appears from the aforesaid evidence that P.Ws. 3, 4 and 7 claimed themselves as eye-witnesses to the occurrence and their names find place in the F.I.R. on this behalf, but from the evidence of P.W.10 the investigating officer it transpires that none of them said about seeing the occurrence directly as alleged. P.W.1 found to have admitted that their house is half a mile off from the place of occurrence and the same is not visible from their house, but there is no explanation as to how she saw the occurrence personally. More so, the evidence of P.Ws. 3, 4 and 7 the alleged eye-witnesses to the occurrence whose names find place in the F.I.R. does not corroborate with the injuries allegedly sustained by the deceased. P.W.5 found to have made out a new story about a gunshot allegedly heard by him during the occurrence which is not the prosecution case that the accused ever used gun during the occurrence for making any gunshot thereto. Furthermore, the evidence of P.Ws. 1 to 8 are contradictory in nature about the injuries allegedly sustained by the deceased. Moreover, P.W.8 was examined by the investigating officer of this case nearly 45 days after the occurrence leaving scope for manipulation of the evidence so produced by the prosecution. 

 16. The most vital aspect of this case is that the medical officer who held post-mortem examination on the dead body of the deceased has not been examined in this case nor his post-mortem examination report has been brought on record as exhibit in compliance with the provisions of Section 509A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. So, in absence of evidence of the doctor who held postmortem examination on the dead body of the deceased as well as the absence of postmortem examination report we are in dark about the injuries so sustained by the deceased during the occurrence. This fact alone led us to hold that the prosecution has hopelessly failed to prove the cause of death of the deceased. Furthermore, the absence of doctor or the post-mortem examination report deprive us to examine the veracity of the private P.Ws. who said on dock about causing of different injuries on different parts of the body of deceased which may have caused the death of the deceased. Furthermore, the evidence of P.Ws. 1 to 8 so far it relates to sustaining of injuries by the deceased at the hands of individual accused appears to have not been corroborated by the P.Ws. and as such their evidence' cannot be relied upon. One thing is very much vital in this case that none of the independent villagers who allegedly came to the place of occurrence and saw/heard the occurrence from other eyewitnesses has not been examined in this case nor any student of the Madrasha which is situated on the bank of P.O. river has been examined in this case and the. prosecution found to be totally silent about their absence and in view of such facts and circumstances we have reasons to hold that had the Madrasha students or the villagers who allegedly saw the occurrence have been examined, would not have supported the prosecution case and in that case the provisions of Section 114 (g) of the Evidence Act may go in favour of the defence. Then comes about the evidence of P.W. 2. This P.W.2 is admittedly inimical with one of the accused-appellants of this case and even his name does not find place in the F.I.R. as witness. So, his evidence may be left out of consideration. 

 17. The up shod of our discussions indicates that none of the P.Ws. examined in this case ever reported about taking of part by the accused-appellants in the occurrence during investigation and as such their evidence should be swallowed with a grain of salt. Finally, the absence of the doctor who held post-mortem examination on the dead body of the deceased together with absence of post mortem examination report which has not been brought on record in compliance with the provisions of Section 509A of the Code of Criminal Procedure we are in dark about the injuries so sustained by the deceased at the hands of the individual accused. as alleged together with the absence of any alamat of this case, specially, any blood stained earth in the face of clear admission of P.W.1 that blood fell down on earth, while the dead body was brought from the river on its bank coupled with bringing a fact about hearing of sound of a gun shot during the occurrence has made the entire prosecution case unworthy to believe and in the result the prosecution case must fail.
